recipes.title: Chinese red-braised pork and eggs, light
recipes.summary: Pork belly and eggs slowly braised with soy sauce, rice wine, ginger and star anise, served with cabbage and a modest portion of rice.

steps.instruction: Prepare the pork belly, green cabbage, ginger, garlic and spring onions in their listed forms.
Stir the soy sauce, rice wine, brown sugar and chicken broth together.
Boil the eggs until firm.
Cool the eggs in cold water.
Peel the eggs.
Cook the white rice until tender and fully steamed.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy saucepan over medium-high heat.
Brown the pork belly until several sides are deeply coloured.
Add the ginger, garlic and star anise to the pork belly.
Pour the soy sauce mixture into the saucepan.
Simmer the covered pork belly until tender and richly seasoned.
Add the peeled eggs to the braising liquid.
Simmer uncovered until the eggs are stained brown and the sauce becomes glossy.
Cook the green cabbage in the braising sauce until tender.
Rest the Chinese red-braised pork and eggs so the sauce settles.
Finish the braise with the spring onions.
Serve the pork belly and eggs with the white rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the braise and rice separately for up to 3 days. Reheat gently until the pork and eggs are steaming. Freeze the pork braise without the eggs for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: French croque monsieur bites, light
recipes.summary: Small baked croque monsieur bites with cured pork, cheddar and a light parmesan béchamel, crisp at the edges and creamy inside.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Prepare the bread, cured pork, cheddar cheese and parmesan cheese in their listed forms.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Stir the wheat flour into the butter until a smooth paste forms.
Pour the whole milk into the saucepan gradually.
Cook the sauce until it thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Stir the parmesan cheese, thyme and salt into the sauce.
Spread the parmesan sauce over half of the bread pieces.
Layer the cured pork and cheddar cheese over the sauced bread.
Cover each stack with a remaining bread piece.
Bake the croque monsieur bites until the cheddar cheese melts and the bread turns crisp and golden.
Rest the French croque monsieur bites briefly before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten warm. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat in a hot oven until the bread is crisp and the cheese is melted. Freeze baked bites for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Greek tomato scrambled eggs, light
recipes.summary: Soft Greek-style scrambled eggs folded through a rich tomato, onion and thyme sauce, served with a modest amount of toasted bread.

steps.instruction: Prepare the bread, onion, garlic and spring onions in their listed forms.
Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the onion until soft and lightly golden.
Stir the garlic and thyme into the onion until fragrant.
Simmer the tomatoes, canned, until thick and no longer watery.
Beat the eggs with the salt until evenly combined.
Pour the eggs into the tomato mixture.
Fold the eggs gently until softly set and still moist.
Toast the bread until crisp and golden.
Rest the Greek tomato scrambled eggs briefly so the texture settles.
Finish the eggs with the spring onions.
Serve the Greek tomato scrambled eggs with the bread.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten immediately. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat gently in a pan. Store the bread separately. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Mexican albondigas soup, light
recipes.summary: A lighter Mexican meatball soup with beef, rice, potatoes, carrots and zucchini in a cumin, tomato and cilantro broth.

steps.instruction: Prepare the potato, carrot, zucchini, onion, garlic, cilantro and lime in their listed forms.
Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Mix the ground beef, eggs, white rice, half the onion, half the garlic, half the cumin, half the paprika and half the salt.
Shape the beef mixture into small round meatballs.
Cook the remaining onion in a large soup pot until soft and translucent.
Stir the remaining garlic, cumin and paprika into the onion until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and vegetable broth to the pot.
Bring the tomato broth to a gentle simmer.
Add the potato and carrot to the simmering broth.
Simmer until the potato and carrot begin to soften.
Lower the meatballs carefully into the broth.
Simmer until the meatballs are cooked through and the white rice inside them is tender.
Add the zucchini to the soup.
Simmer until the zucchini is tender.
Stir the cilantro and remaining salt into the soup.
Serve the Mexican albondigas soup with the lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat gently until the meatballs are steaming. Freeze the soup for up to 2 months; the potato and zucchini will soften.

recipes.title: Indian coconut cod curry, light
recipes.summary: Cod simmered in a light coconut, tomato, ginger and cumin sauce with spinach and peppers, served with a modest portion of rice.

steps.instruction: Prepare the cod, bell pepper, onion, garlic, ginger and cilantro in their listed forms.
Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender and fully steamed.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide saucepan over medium heat.
Cook the onion until soft and lightly golden.
Stir the garlic, ginger, cumin, paprika and salt into the onion until fragrant.
Cook the bell pepper until it begins to soften.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and coconut milk to the saucepan.
Simmer the curry sauce until slightly thickened.
Fold the spinach into the sauce until wilted.
Simmer the cod gently in the curry until opaque and flaky at the thickest point.
Stir the lemon juice into the curry.
Finish the Indian coconut cod curry with the cilantro.
Serve the cod curry with the white rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the curry and rice separately for up to 2 days. Reheat gently until the cod is hot without boiling hard. Freezing is not recommended.
